method.scope: All 20 seconds of both actual decoded movies reviewed chronologically at 6 fps, with native-resolution spot checks. Final rerender changed only ending type size/placement and interpretive heading scale; that complete changed 16–20s region was freshly decoded and reviewed. Earlier unchanged composition review is retained.

comparison.overall: The experiment is a meaningful visual improvement in typography, spatial movement, dimensional graphics and transition staging. It is not an unconditional win in every dimension: the baseline is more uniform for reading and its fractured red numerals feel more scarred and gritty.
merits: The rotating thick rings and slanted red forms add depth and visible motion without displacing active words.
Camera travel leads from grief to vengeance, Cain, Lamech and the large 77; pauses leave time to read between the moves.
Large expressive keywords, narrow uppercase accents and restrained italic connectors provide much stronger hierarchy than the baseline single treatment.
The red 77 grows through an impact-ring burst, turns pale, separates and reveals the Christ image. This is a clearer continuous transformation than the baseline hard scene change.
The photoreal Christ remains solid and human, and the restrained white finish supports the mercy interpretation.
tradeoffs: The new geometry and smooth solid lettering look cleaner and more like modern motion posters; the baseline fractured numerals communicate physical violence more directly.
Mixed type sizes and moving spatial groups require slightly more visual tracking than the baseline consistently placed uppercase text.
Several short camera transitions have no visible lyric; they occur between phrase groups, with no sustained dead opening or long empty hold observed.

resolvedFinding.issue: Initial ending made the sung Adam/Eve lyric markedly smaller than the interpretation heading.
resolvedFinding.correction: Sung lyric enlarged and moved into a clear bottom band; interpretation heading reduced.
resolvedFinding.verification: All 24 final ending samples plus a native-resolution frame show clear, unclipped lyrics with sufficient separation from Christ and the interpretation. No further revision required for this experiment.

scoresOutOf10.qualification: Subjective visual scores for this 20-second excerpt only. Pacing score concerns visible motion/hold balance, not a claim of listening or beat accuracy.

limitations: No subjective hearing or sung-word alignment judgment was performed by this reviewer. Audio, timing and OCR checks are owned by the main review.
Sampling at 6 fps cannot rule out every one-frame artifact or establish full-speed perceived smoothness.
This comparison demonstrates what the authored experiment achieves; it does not establish that a different renderer automatically creates better art.
No claim is made about the unmodified remainder of the full song or phone playback.
